page: Google Cloud Platform c4-standard-24 is a general-purpose server instance powered by an Intel Xeon 8581C processor. It features 24 vCPUs mapped to 12 physical cores with hyper-threading enabled, running at a base clock speed of 2.3 GHz. The instance is equipped with 90 GB of system memory, providing a resource density of 3.75 GB per vCPU. It does not include local storage or bundled GPUs, and does not offer complimentary public IPv4 addresses.

The underlying Intel Xeon architecture includes advanced instruction sets such as AVX-512 and Intel Advanced Matrix Extensions (AMX) for tile and INT8 operations. These hardware accelerators contribute to notable performance in specific workloads. In benchmark testing, the instance achieved a top-tier result in LLM inference text generation for a small 135M model, reaching 396.71 tokens per second. Text processing benchmarks also showed strong performance, scoring 2618.0 in Geekbench.

Other performance metrics, such as stress-ng single-core (1811.68) and multi-core (21669.81) CPU tests, fall within the average range. Memory bandwidth is measured at 1681.44 GB/sec for cached small blocks and 139.38 GB/sec for uncached large blocks. The instance is qualitatively cost-efficient for workloads that leverage its advanced vector and matrix instruction sets without requiring local SSD storage or dedicated GPU hardware. It is suited for general-purpose workloads, software compilation, text processing, and lightweight machine learning inference.

Operating at 2.3 GHz across 12 physical cores with hyper-threading, this x86_64 architecture includes 260 MB of L3 cache and supports advanced instruction sets like AVX-512 and Intel AMX. The instance does not feature local storage or bundled GPUs. Performance benchmarks indicate average multi-core CPU capabilities alongside strong text processing and top-tier small-model LLM text generation speeds of 396.71 tokens per second. This profile makes the c4-standard-24 qualitatively cost-efficient for balanced workloads, software compilation, and CPU-based machine learning inference that do not require local NVMe storage.
